sources.quote: Mamluk generals used their power to establish a dynasty that ruled Egypt and Syria from 1250 to 1517.
The Ayyubid decline in Egypt was completed with the Mamluk accession to power following the battle at Al-Manṣūrah (1250), but the dynasty persisted in some areas of Syria until 1260
Such was the birth of the Mamluk dynasty (May 1250).
a treaty was concluded (April 1253) between Aybeg and an-Nasir, by which the former would hold Egypt and a slice of Palestine at the banks of the Jordan, including Jerusalem as well as the coastline
In September of 1260, at 'Ain Jālūt, the Mamluks crushed Kitbogha, and occupied almost all of Syria.

notes.en: Ziada (1969) says that under a treaty of April 1253 the Mamluk ruler Aybeg held Egypt and 'a slice of Palestine' to the Jordan, including Jerusalem and the coast. The map does not show this yet because it rests on one source; it should be checked against Humphreys (1977).
notes.ar: يقول زيادة (1969) إنه بموجب معاهدة نيسان/أبريل 1253 احتفظ الحاكم المملوكي أيبك بمصر و«شريحة من فلسطين» حتى نهر الأردن، بما فيها القدس والساحل. ولا تُظهر الخريطة ذلك بعد لأنه يستند إلى مصدر واحد؛ وينبغي التحقق منه مقابل همفريز (1977).
notes.he: זיאדה (1969) אומר שלפי הסכם מאפריל 1253 החזיק השליט הממלוכי איבכ במצרים וב"רצועה של פלשתינה" עד הירדן, כולל ירושלים והחוף. המפה עדיין אינה מציגה זאת משום שהדבר נשען על מקור אחד; יש לבדוק אותו מול האמפריז (1977).

description.en: Former Syrian Ayyubid lands occupied after Ayn Jalut; the Frankish coast reduced step by step (Caesarea, Haifa, Arsuf 1265; Safed/Galilee 1266) until Acre fell in 1291.
description.ar: أراضي الأيوبيين السوريين السابقة التي احتُلت بعد عين جالوت؛ وتقلص الساحل الفرنجي خطوة خطوة (قيسارية وحيفا وأرسوف 1265؛ صفد/الجليل 1266) حتى سقطت عكا عام 1291.
description.he: אדמות האיובים הסורים לשעבר שנכבשו לאחר עין ג׳אלות; החוף הפרנקי הצטמצם צעד אחר צעד (קיסריה, חיפה וארסוף 1265; צפת/הגליל 1266) עד נפילת עכו ב-1291.

sources.quote: When the Mongol cataclysm of 658/1260 destroyed the Syrian Ayyubid kingdom of al-Nāṣer, the Mamluk regime was able to occupy his former dominions.
decisive victory of the Mamluks of Egypt over the invading Mongols on September 3, 1260
In 1265 he took Caesarea, Haifa, and Arsuf. The following year he conquered Galilee
Safed passed from hand to hand during the Crusades until captured by Baybars I, who razed its citadel (1266).
during whose reign the last of the Crusaders were driven out of Acre (May 18, 1291).
In September of 1260, at 'Ain Jālūt, the Mamluks crushed Kitbogha, and occupied almost all of Syria.
In this way he extended the suzerainty of the Mamluk sultanate over Syria and Palestine, except for the small principality of Kerak.
Eventually Baybars had him entrapped, and sent him a prisoner to the citadel of Cairo, where he was executed on a charge of treasonable correspondence with the Mongols (April 1263).
He began by capturing the ports of Caesarea, Haifa, and Arsuf, razing their fortifications to the ground
In 1266 he gave orders for intensive raids against the crusader towns along the Syrian coast, while he himself took Safad
Early in 1268 he again went to Syria, where he took Jaffa, Belfort, and, after a strenuous siege, Antioch
The final assault took place in the early morning of Friday, May 18, 1291

notes.en: After 'Ain Jalut the Mamluks held Syria and Palestine except the small Ayyubid principality of Kerak (Ziada 1969), whose prince al-Mughith was seized by Baybars and executed in April 1263; moab/edom/madaba-plain could therefore be full units from 1263. Galilee units partial until the conquest of Galilee (Safad) in 1266.
notes.ar: بعد عين جالوت سيطر المماليك على سوريا وفلسطين باستثناء إمارة الكرك الأيوبية الصغيرة (زيادة 1969)، التي اعتقل بيبرس أميرها المغيث وأعدمه في نيسان/أبريل 1263؛ ولذلك يمكن أن تكون وحدات مؤاب وأدوم وسهل مأدبا وحدات كاملة منذ 1263. وحدات الجليل جزئية حتى فتح الجليل (صفد) سنة 1266.
notes.he: אחרי עין ג'אלות החזיקו הממלוכים בסוריה ובפלשתינה, מלבד הנסיכות האיובית הקטנה של כרכ (זיאדה 1969), שנסיכה אל־מע'ית' נתפס בידי בייברס והוצא להורג באפריל 1263; לכן היחידות מואב, אדום ומישור מידבא יכולות להיות יחידות מלאות מ־1263. יחידות הגליל חלקיות עד כיבוש הגליל (צפת) ב־1266.

description.en: Whole of Palestine, Transjordan and southern Syria, governed through provinces centred on Damascus, Safad, Gaza and Karak.
description.ar: كامل فلسطين وشرق الأردن وجنوب سوريا، تُحكم عبر ولايات مركزها دمشق وصفد وغزة والكرك.
description.he: כל פלשתינה, עבר הירדן ודרום סוריה, נשלטים באמצעות מחוזות שמרכזיהם דמשק, צפת, עזה וכרך.

sources.quote: during whose reign the last of the Crusaders were driven out of Acre (May 18, 1291).
Palestine formed a part of the district of Damascus, second only to Egypt in the Mamluk domains.
In the north was the niyābah or mamlakah – both of which can be translated as “province” in this context – of Ṣafad, including areas in modern-day southern Lebanon and the Golan Heights.
Gaza was the province in the southwest of the country: about two thirds up the coast to Haifa, and inland as far as Bayt Jibrīl.
the second tier cities of the Sultanate in Syria: Hama, Homs, Tripoli, Karak and Safad.

notes.en: Interrupted by the Mongol occupation of Damascus and raids in Palestine in 1299-1300 (see ilkhanate). Desert margins partial.
notes.ar: انقطعت باحتلال المغول لدمشق والغارات في فلسطين في 1299-1300 (انظر ilkhanate). هوامش الصحراء جزئية.
notes.he: נקטעה בכיבוש המונגולי של דמשק ובפשיטות בפלשתינה ב-1299-1300 (ראו ilkhanate). שולי המדבר חלקיים.

description.en: Egypt (Sinai) after the loss of Syria and Palestine, until the Ottoman victory at Raydaniyya.
description.ar: مصر (سيناء) بعد فقدان سوريا وفلسطين، حتى الانتصار العثماني في الريدانية.
description.he: מצרים (סיני) לאחר אובדן סוריה ופלשתינה, עד הניצחון העות׳מאני בריידאניה.

sources.quote: Selim defeated the Mamluk armies at the battles of Marj Dābiq (north of Aleppo; August 24, 1516) and Raydāniyyah (near Cairo; January 22, 1517), thus bringing Syria, Egypt, and Palestine under Ottoman rule.
on August 24, 1516, when the Ottoman sultan Selim I routed the Mamluk armies at the Battle of Marj Dābiq. Palestine began its four centuries under Ottoman domination.
After Marj Dabiq, Selim I's army advanced southward, and Syria passed quickly into the possession of the Ottomans, whose advent was in many places welcomed as meaning deliverance from the Mamluks.
came the bad news that the army that had gone to Gaza had suffered defeat on Sunday, the 24th, of Dhu'l Ka'dah.

the Mamluk army was defeated first near Gaza, and then at Raidaniyah outside Cairo. The latter battle was fought in January 1517, and on the next day Selim I was recognized as sultan of Egypt and Syria
Tumanbey II continued the struggle for some months, but was finally vanquished and, after being captured, was executed in April 1517. With his death the proud empire of the Mamluks came to an end.

notes.en: Palestine was lost before Egypt: the Mamluk army sent to Gaza was defeated in December 1516 (Ibn Iyas: Sunday 24 Dhu l-Qa'da 922). Ziada dates the end of the Mamluk state to the execution of Tumanbay II in April 1517.
notes.ar: فُقدت فلسطين قبل مصر: هُزم الجيش المملوكي المرسل إلى غزة في كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1516 (ابن إياس: الأحد 24 ذي القعدة 922). ويؤرخ زيادة نهاية الدولة المملوكية بإعدام طومان باي الثاني في نيسان/أبريل 1517.
notes.he: פלשתינה אבדה לפני מצרים: הצבא הממלוכי שנשלח לעזה הובס בדצמבר 1516 (אבן איאס: יום ראשון, 24 בד'ו אל־קעדה 922). זיאדה מתארך את סוף המדינה הממלוכית להוצאתו להורג של טומאנבאי השני באפריל 1517.
